parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text:
The equation of state for an ideal gas may be written as
pVA = NBT
where p is the pressure of the gas, V is the volume of the gas, A is the Avogadro constant, B
is another constant and N is the number of molecules of the gas.
parts.question_text_latex:

where p is the pressure of the gas, V is the volume of the gas, A is the Avogadro constant, B
is another constant and N is the number of molecules of the gas.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
The product pV for an ideal gas is also given by
pV = (1)/(3) Nm 〈 c^{2}〉 .
parts.question_text_latex:
The product pV for an ideal gas is also given by
$pV = \frac{1}{3} Nm \langle c^{2}\rangle .$

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.question_text: State the meanings, in this equation, of the symbols m and 〈 c^{2}〉.
parts.question_text_latex: State the meanings, in this equation, of the symbols m and $\langle c^{2}\rangle$.
